claim_boundary: This artifact compiles each represented difference into a common rational multiplier and quantifies chain depth and phase error. It proves no long chain from energy alone, seed realization, low-multiplicity bound, simple-root closure, complete moment, density, or intervals.

freiman_recurrence_theorem.anchor_gate: the recurrence retains d,rho_d and rational labels, but E16 must still tie one chain vertex to the original packet anchor and verify that the required depth is supplied
freiman_recurrence_theorem.approximation: rho_d=g^d(1+O(1/(KQ))); on a supported J<=D chain, rho_d^J=g^(Jd)(1+O(J/(KQ))) and the worst total error is O(D/(KQ))=X^(-(xi-4/15)+o(1))
freiman_recurrence_theorem.boundary: no long chain follows from energy alone; no seed realization, low-multiplicity bound, simple-root closure, complete moment, density, or prime intervals is proved
freiman_recurrence_theorem.chain_bound: the d-edge graph is a disjoint union of paths; with R vertices and L_d edges, one path has at least ceil(L_d/(R-L_d)) edges
freiman_recurrence_theorem.depth_gate: L_d>=ceil(JR/(J+1)) is sufficient for a J-edge chain; popular-edge pigeonholing alone does not approach this density unless A is nearly full
freiman_recurrence_theorem.difference_multiplier: for E_d={a in A:a+d in A}, Freiman multiplicativity applied to (a+d)+b=a+(b+d) makes rho_d=r_(a+d)/r_a independent of a in E_d
freiman_recurrence_theorem.geometric_chain: on a chain a0,a0+d,...,a0+Jd, one has exactly r_(a0+jd)=r_a0 rho_d^j
freiman_recurrence_theorem.popular_difference: if A has R points in D consecutive integers, some nonzero d has L_d>=ceil(R(R-1)/(2D-2)) oriented edges

remaining_target.statement: force near-unit edge density for a represented difference or obtain the required E16 anchor/depth by a different graph extraction
